title: Sample 13-1: Centered Poem

illustrates.quote: Poems that are centered on the print page use 1-3 margins or are treated as displayed material and use the margin in effect. (See Sample 13-1: Centered Poem on page 13-13.)

blocks.text: Presented here is a familiar example from one of Donne’s songs:
blocks.features: Introductory lead-in sentence, ordinary paragraph, before the centered poem.
Nine lines from John Donne's "The Bait" (originally titled "Song"), centered as a block on the print page (each line's own horizontal centre roughly aligned, not flush to a common left margin).

lines.text: Go and catch a falling star,
Get with child a mandrake root,
Tell me where all times past are,
Or who cleft the Devil’s foot;
Teach me to hear mermaids singing,
Or to keep off envy's stinging,
Serves to advance an honest mind.

print.notes: Picture on PDF p.367; the poem is visually centred as a block (per this example's title) rather than left-justified.
print.printFeatures: Plain body-text serif font; poem block visually centred under the lead-in sentence.

braille.notes: Verbatim from .txt lines 10663-10674 (a genuine excerpt: the sample's own printed line numbers begin at 10, i.e. lines 1-9 of this braille page belong to preceding, unshown content), after stripping a 5-character line-number field (2-digit max line number 21, + 3 = 5) and converting U+2800 blank cells to spaces. Line 3 above is the blank line (line 12 in the source) between the lead-in sentence and the poem. All nine poem lines (originally numbered 13-21) carry a uniform 2-cell indent (cell 3) -- i.e. the whole poem is transcribed at a flush cell-3 margin throughout, matching rule 13.3.1.c's alternative 'treated as displayed material and use the margin in effect' option, rather than the ordinary 1-3 main/runover margin (which would put line-initial cells at column 1, not 3).

uncertain: Whether the source intends the cell-3 flush margin as 'displayed material...margin in effect' or as some other convention is not stated explicitly in the rule text; inferred from the measured, uniform 2-cell indent on every poem line (no line starts at cell 1).
